decisions.reason: As a very recent launch in a metal-infrastructure niche, the firm is likely to give the pipe cleaning box more time because development and market-entry costs are already sunk and slow municipal uptake can still be seen as temporary.

Public waste bins fit the firm's fabricated-metal capabilities and public website promotion creates visible commitment, so management would likely persist despite any weak first-year sales, though competition makes pruning somewhat more plausible than for core line extensions.

Ground sleeves appear close to the firm's core metal products and, having just been introduced, are likely to be retained while management justifies the investment and waits for broader customer adoption.

Cast iron ground sleeves look like a committed extension of the ground-sleeve range, and because they reinforce an announced product family the firm is likely to keep them on the market rather than reverse course quickly.

Steel ground sleeves are also a close-to-core line extension, so escalation of commitment and the ease of blaming any early shortfall on normal ramp-up effects make continued marketing the most likely choice.
